api/GameEventScript.Api.GesRuntimeLimits.title: Class GesRuntimeLimits | Game Event Script C# API — Unreleased (47afc43b2fc1)
api/GameEventScript.Api.GesRuntimeLimits.summary: Class GesRuntimeLimits Namespace GameEventScript.Api Assembly GameEventScript.Runtime.dll The safety limits of one host: work, nesting and collection sizes per handler and the queue of the host. They bound time and stack use, not memory (specs/HostRuntime.md). Exceeding most limits stops the active handler with a structured runtime-limit observation; the remarks of each property state its exact outcome. public sealed class GesRuntimeLimits Inheritance object GesRuntimeLimits Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Constructors GesRuntimeLimits() public GesRuntimeLimits() Properties Default A shared instance with the default limits of every property. public static GesRuntimeLimits Default { get; } Property Value GesRuntimeLimits MaxCallDepth Specifies the maximum nesting of function and predicate calls in one handler. public int MaxCallDepth { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 64. Unlike the other limits, zero is not "disabled": it permits only root handlers, so a Program that calls a function or predicate fails Load with link.requiredCallStackDepthExceeded. Values are clamped to the encoded u16 range. Call graphs are acyclic, so Load checks the Program's static depth. MaxDiceCount Specifies the maximum number of dice one roll may create. public int MaxDiceCount { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 1,000; a nonpositive value disables the limit. A larger roll yields empty Dice and reports this limit to the observer; the handler continues. MaxDiceSides Specifies the maximum number of sides of one die. public int MaxDiceSides { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 1,000,000; a nonpositive value disables the limit. A roll with more sides yields empty Dice and reports this limit to the observer; the handler continues. MaxExecutionSteps Specifies the maximum number of opcodes one script handler may execute. public int MaxExecutionSteps { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 100,000; a nonpositive value disables the limit. The count persists across frame pauses and resets for each handler. Exactly the limit is allowed; a handler that would execute more stops with this limit. MaxGeneratedCollectionItems Specifies the maximum size of each collection incrementally materialized by generated lists and iterator-backed selectors. public int MaxGeneratedCollectionItems { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 10,000; a nonpositive value disables this limit. Counts include retained nothing items, but exclude discarded duplicates and skipped map keys. Grouping limits the number of groups and each group's size independently. Before an insertion would exceed the limit, the runtime rejects it and stops the handler without returning a partial result. Separate collections have separate size limits; this property does not bound existing inputs or allocated bytes. MaxLoopIterations Specifies the maximum number of successful iterator advances across loops and iterator-backed selectors in one handler. public int MaxLoopIterations { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 100,000; a nonpositive value disables this limit. A present nothing item counts, but iterator exhaustion does not. Exactly the limit is allowed; the next successful advance stops the handler before its body or selector expression executes. The counter persists across frame pauses and resets for each handler. MaxProcessedMessagesPerRun Specifies the maximum number of logical messages completed by a pump before it stops with a processing-limit result while more messages remain queued. public int MaxProcessedMessagesPerRun { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 64; a nonpositive value disables this limit. Each message counts once, after all captured handlers finish. Exactly reaching the limit while draining the queue completes normally. Otherwise pending messages remain queued for a later pump call. MaxQueuedMessages Specifies the maximum number of logical messages a host may hold queued, delayed entries included. public int MaxQueuedMessages { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 0, which like every nonpositive value disables the limit. When it is reached, an Emit or Publish statement and a native Emit or Publish drop the local message, report the limit to the observer and continue; a result-bearing or delayed send stops its handler with this limit; an initialization snapshot that finds no slot fails Load with link.initializationQueueFull. MaxRandomScopeDepth Defines the maximum number of simultaneously active nested random scopes owned by one host. public int MaxRandomScopeDepth { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The lazily initialized scope storage provides this many regular states plus one internal fault-gate state. Reaching the configured depth is valid; attempting one additional push faults the current handler without changing the parent random stream. The value must be between 0 and 65,535. MaxRangeItems Specifies the maximum number of items a Range may enumerate or materialize. public int MaxRangeItems { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 10,000; a nonpositive value disables the limit. A loop over a longer Range runs no iteration, and a List cast or shuffle of one yields an empty List; each reports this limit to the observer while the handler continues. Inside parse the limit bounds the total of all Ranges it materializes and stops the handler. MaxRegisterValues Specifies the maximum number of values in the reusable VM register storage of one host. public int MaxRegisterValues { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 512; a nonpositive value selects that portable default. Load rejects a Program whose declared register requirement exceeds it. MaxValueDepth Specifies the maximum nesting depth of a List, Map, Record or Message that a handler constructs. public int MaxValueDepth { get; init; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 64; a nonpositive value disables this limit. A List, Map, Record or Message is one level deeper than its deepest item, field or argument, and every other value has depth 0, so a List of numbers has depth 1. Constructing a deeper value stops the handler with this runtime limit. The bound keeps the recursive conversion, comparison and release of script-built values within the native stack. Values that native code builds through the API are not checked until a handler nests them further.

api/GameEventScript.Api.html.title: Namespace GameEventScript.Api | Game Event Script C# API — Unreleased (47afc43b2fc1)
api/GameEventScript.Api.html.summary: Namespace GameEventScript.Api Classes GameEventScriptHost Serial message host for native handlers and optional GameEventScript programs. The portable core performs no synchronization and creates no worker threads. GameEventScriptMessage Represents a message used within the Game Event Script system. This message serves as a fundamental unit for communication, allowing for event-driven execution between components, scripts, and handlers. GameEventScriptProgram The immutable, reusable parsed representation of one .gesb V1 program, produced only by the Compiler or by Read(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, GesProgramReadOptions?), both of which run the complete program validator before returning it. GesBinaryFormat Fixed constants of the canonical little-endian .gesb V1 container framing. GesBoundNetwork A network bound to parameter values. Immutable; it can be shared between threads and connections. GesBoundSchema A schema, message or message set bound to parameter values. Immutable; it can be shared between threads. GesBuildMetadataSegment The immutable optional BuildMetadataSegment (section 0x0030), which names the producing compiler. Runtime behaviour never depends on it. GesCompileException Represents an exception that occurs during the compilation process of a Game Event Script. This exception is specifically used to signal issues detected during the parsing or validation phase of script compilation. GesCompileOptions Represents a game event script compile options. GesContext Host-owned context shared by native and GameEventScript handlers. GesDebugSymbolsSegment The immutable optional DebugSymbolsSegment (section 0x0020), which names script parameters and locals by register and code range. Runtime behaviour never depends on it. GesDeclaredExternalTypeCatalog Immutable external type catalog built from a fixed list of definitions. GesDiagnostic A portable diagnostic of a source, binary, linking or runtime failure. Phase and Code identify it; the optional fields add structured context and are absent when unknown. GesDiagnosticCodes Defines the stable diagnostic code strings; a code is compared together with its GesDiagnosticPhase, never through the message text. GesDocument An immutable GES document: a Map or Record root with an optional schema reference, read from and printed to human-editable .gesd text. Comments and layout are not part of a document. GesDocumentException GES document text is invalid or exceeds a fixed literal parsing limit. GesDocumentFormat Layout options for printing GES documents and values. Layout is a recommendation: every printed document reads back to an equal document, while indentation, line breaks and numeric spelling may differ between implementations. GesDocumentSchema The schema reference of a GES document. It is a reference only: GES neither loads schema files nor validates documents against record definitions. GesDynamicLinkException Thrown when a Program cannot be linked to a host, for example because of a missing extension or external type constructor or an exceeded register or call-depth limit. It carries one or more link-phase diagnostics. GesExtensionCall Reusable call-scoped adapter passed to Invoke(GesExtensionCall): it lends the arguments, the host context and its random generator, and receives one result. The last setter call before the callback returns decides the result; without one the result is Nothing. The call must not be retained. GesExtensionFaultException A deliberate, portable runtime fault that an extension function, native handler, external-type constructor, or IGesExternalValue implementation throws to report a defined failure. It ends the current handler with a diagnosable runtime error instead of silently evaluating to nothing; the host remains reusable for subsequently enqueued messages, as for any other runtime error. GesExtensionReference Represents an immutable normalized extension name, function name, and ordered argument signature. GesExternalTypeConstructorCall Reusable call-scoped adapter passed to Invoke(GesExternalTypeConstructorCall): it lends the arguments and receives the constructed value. It must not be retained beyond the callback. GesExternalTypeConstructorDefinition Immutable declarative signature of one external type constructor: the type it builds and its parameters. GesExternalTypeConstructorReference Represents an immutable normalized external type name and constructor argument signature. GesExternalTypeDefinition Immutable declarative description of one external type: its name, ordered unique fields and ordered unique constructor signatures. GesExternalTypeFieldDefinition Immutable description of one external type field: its name and declared type. Field values are converted to the declared builtin type before a script sees them; Nothing stays Nothing. GesExternalTypeParameterDefinition Immutable description of one external constructor parameter: its argument label, which must name a declared field, and its declared type. Arguments are converted to the declared builtin type before the constructor sees them; Nothing stays Nothing. GesFatalRuntimeException Base class of exceptions that carry a runtime GesDiagnostic and end the current handler with that diagnostic. The exception message is the diagnostic's message. GesFloatRange An immutable binary64 range descriptor; terms are computed lazily. GesGeometryLibrary The standard geometry library: the external types :Box, :Poly and :Disc over GesBox, GesPoly and GesDisc, and the extension functions :geometry.*, so that hosts and scripts compute alike. A host that wants it passes Catalog(IGesExternalTypeCatalog?) to the compiler and ExternalTypes(IGesExternalTypeRegistry?) and Extensions(IGesExtensionRegistry?) to the host, each in front of its own catalog or registry, which resolves what the library does not. GesHostBuilder Configures and creates independent serial GameEventScriptHost instances. GesIntegerRange An immutable signed-64 range descriptor. Terms are computed lazily without binary64 conversion. GesLiteralLimitException Literal recognition outside a Host exceeded one of its fixed protection limits. GesMessageArguments Ordered message arguments. Argument names are part of the message signature and therefore preserve source order. GesMessageFormatException Invalid, unsupported, or over-limit portable message/value JSON. GesMessageSignature Represents a message signature used in GameEventScript to uniquely define the structure of a message, including its name and ordered parameter list. This class provides utilities to normalize, validate, and match message signatures accurately. GesNetwork A network declaration: the routes of one client–server pair. Immutable; it can be bound any number of times. GesNetworkRoute One route of a network. Immutable. GesOpaqueSection An optional section the reader retained without interpreting it under PreserveAll: an unknown optional section, or a known optional section with an unsupported version or compression. The writer re-emits it unchanged after the known sections. GesPoly A closed polygon in the plane z = 0, without a unit: its points in order, the last connecting to the first. A polygon is valid with at least three finite points in the plane, no edge of zero length, no two edges that cross or overlap, and an area other than zero; the operations of an invalid one give null, as GES operations give nothing for a domain failure. Scripts see it as the external type :Poly of GesGeometryLibrary. GesProgramBuilder Compiles source text into immutable Programs using the optional GameEventScript.Compiler package. GesProgramBuilderEntry Adds the Program builder entry point to GameEventScriptProgram when the Compiler package is referenced. GesProgramFormatException Thrown when a .gesb image or a program is malformed, unsupported, exceeds read limits, or violates a program invariant. Raised by reading, writing, size calculation, validation and Host.Load. GesProgramInstance Represents one host-local loading of a reusable immutable program. GesProgramReadLimits Resource bounds that Read(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, GesProgramReadOptions?) checks before allocating. Exceeding a count limit fails with TooManyEntries, a byte limit with the code named on the property; a limit outside its supported range makes Read throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException. GesProgramReadOptions Options for Read(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, GesProgramReadOptions?). GesQuantityUnits Names, spellings and arithmetic of the closed set of GameEventScript quantity units. GesRandomGenerator A sealed class that provides mechanisms for generating random numbers or values, either through a pseudo-random number generator or a predefined sequence of values. This class is useful for scenarios where deterministic or non-deterministic random value generation is required, especially in game event scripts. GesRuntimeLimits The safety limits of one host: work, nesting and collection sizes per handler and the queue of the host. They bound time and stack use, not memory (specs/HostRuntime.md). Exceeding most limits stops the active handler with a structured runtime-limit observation; the remarks of each property state its exact outcome. GesSchema The immutable description of one schema, message or message set of a GesSchemaSet. It can be shared between threads and bound any number of times. GesSchemaAxisInfo The limits of a numeric axis of a Point, Vector, Box, Poly or Disc, or of the radius of a Disc. GesSchemaComputedFieldInfo A field written computed by: a value derived from the other fields that is never encoded or read from a document. GesSchemaConstantInfo A constant of a schema, declared as let name be value: never encoded, part of the hash, and generated as a static member of the schema's types. GesSchemaDefaultEntryInfo A field that a record literal default names, with its value. GesSchemaDefaultInfo The value a field takes when a value or document leaves it out, declared with default; the wire always carries the field. GesSchemaDelta Converts between full records of a schema and deltas against a baseline, the full record the receiver already holds. Both directions compare wire values and allocate nothing on success. Data is untrusted: every limit is checked, and invalid data fails with a GesWireException. GesSchemaDocument A GES document read against the schema its header names, as generated models read their documents: the header :Schema(:Name) names one of the expected schemas, the document passes the schema's check, and its entries are the plain value that a model converts. Errors carry their position and field path. GesSchemaDump Makes binary data readable through a bound schema. GesSchemaException A schema source or a binding that breaks a rule. Callers branch on Code, a stable schema.* code; the message is informative text. GesSchemaFieldInfo A field of a schema or an argument of a message. GesSchemaParameterInfo A parameter that a declaration reaches and every binding must supply. GesSchemaParameters The parameter values of one binding. GesSchemaSet Validated schema sources. A set is immutable and can be bound any number of times, also with different parameter values within one session. GesSchemaTakeInfo The fields a schema takes from another with with. GesSchemaType The type of a field, or one alternative of a union. GesSchemaValues The convenient path between GES values and the wire, for rare data. A Record or Map encodes by field name, and fields without a schema entry, such as computed fields, are not transmitted. Only a Map that selects a union alternative must have a field for each of its keys. Time-critical code uses GesSchemaWriter and GesSchemaReader. GesSourceArchiveEntry One embedded compiler input in the GesSourceArchiveSegment: the exact logical source as UTF-8, without the original byte order mark or file encoding. GesSourceArchiveSegment The immutable optional SourceArchiveSegment (section 0x0022), which embeds the compiler inputs. GesSourceLocation Represents a specific location in a source file or module for the GameEventScript compiler. This class is used to pinpoint the origin of a particular piece of code or error within a source context. GesSourceMapSegment The immutable optional SourceMapSegment (section 0x0021), which maps code addresses to source byte ranges. It is useful without an embedded GesSourceArchiveSegment; when both are present they must agree. GesSourceMapSource Describes one compiler input in the GesSourceMapSegment. All offsets and lengths count bytes of the logical UTF-8 source, not UTF-16 code units. GesSubscription Represents one host-local native message subscription. GesSystemClock The system monotonic clock, measured from the moment the instance was created. Reading allocates nothing and is unaffected by changes of the wall-clock time. An instance may be shared between hosts and network ends that use one timeline. GesVirtualClock A virtual clock for deterministic simulation and tests: its time changes only through Advance(long). Not thread-safe; one caller at a time, like the host or end that reads it. GesWireException A value that cannot be encoded, or data that is not a valid encoding. The error names the field path and holds no value from the data, so it can be logged safely. GesWireRules The value rules of the schema wire format over plain operands: Text and tag validity, the exact quantization of a step p / 10^k and wrapping. Generated schema code calls them with constant operands, and the interpreted writer and reader use the same rules, so both encode identical bytes. Structs GesBindingSegment The immutable BindingSegment (section 0x0004): the program's exported handlers and callables, imported extensions and external types, outbound message signatures and Record constructors, in encoded order. GesBindingSegment.Entry One immutable binding record. In .gesb the argument-name and tag lists are UInt16IndexListSegment indices; this model holds their resolved elements, which are string-constant indices. GesBitReader Reads values of 0 to 64 bits from untrusted data in the bit order of the schema wire format: least significant bit first, bytes in Little Endian order. It knows no schema; generated schema code and GesSchemaReader build on it. Reading allocates nothing. GesBitWriter Writes values of 0 to 64 bits into a caller's buffer in the bit order of the schema wire format: least significant bit first, bytes in Little Endian order. It knows no schema; generated schema code and GesSchemaWriter build on it. Writing allocates nothing. GesBox An axis-aligned box between two corners, without a unit. Creating one orders its corners, so Min is never above Max on an axis; a 2D box has Z 0 on both. Scripts see it as the external type :Box of GesGeometryLibrary. GesBytecodeInstruction One logical bytecode instruction: an opcode, a unit-and-flags byte, three 16-bit operand words and a 64-bit payload, encoded as 16 bytes in .gesb. The named properties are opcode-specific views of the same words; the in-memory layout does not define the encoding. GesCodeSegment The immutable CodeSegment (section 0x0010): the program's single linear instruction table of at most 65,535 instructions, each encoded as 16 bytes. A code address is the zero-based index of an instruction in this table. GesDebugSymbol Names one physical register over a half-open range of code addresses. Only explicit script parameters and locals are named; compiler temporaries are not. GesDisc A filled circle in the plane z = 0, without a unit: a centre and a radius. Creating one takes the radius's magnitude. A disc is valid with a finite centre in the plane and a finite radius; the operations of an invalid one give null, as GES operations give nothing for a domain failure. Scripts see it as the external type :Disc of GesGeometryLibrary. GesExecutionResult Provides an allocation-free summary of one host pump. GesMessageArgument One named value in an ordered message argument list. GesPoint A position with three Binary64 components and no unit, the native counterpart of a GES Point. A 2D point has Z 0. As in the language, a point moves by a GesVector, two points give a vector, and a point does not scale. The unit belongs to the schema or host and is applied when it converts to or from a GesValue. GesProgramMetadataSegment The immutable decoded ProgramMetadataSegment (section 0x0001) of a .gesb V1 program: module identity, program-level resource bounds and the application-owned program version. GesPublishResult Describes the independent local and outbound outcomes of one publish operation without allocating. GesReadOnlyArray<T> Immutable array view used by portable programs and other immutable API models. GesSchemaBound A bound, step or delta range: a parameter or an exact decimal. GesSchemaDecoded A decoded top-level value and the bytes it occupied. GesSchemaDeltaDecoded The sizes of a decoded delta. GesSchemaDumpResult The readable form of encoded data. GesSchemaField The handle of a field in a bound schema. Resolving it once makes further uses free of lookups. GesSchemaReader Decodes one top-level record or message without allocating on success. Data is untrusted: every limit is checked, and invalid data fails with a GesWireException. Fields are read in declaration order. GesSchemaSource A named schema source text. GesSchemaWriter Encodes one top-level record or message into a caller's buffer without allocating on success. Fields are written in declaration order; a nested schema, Point or Vector is entered with BeginNested(GesSchemaField). GesSourceMapEntry Maps a half-open range of code addresses to a range of UTF-8 bytes in one source. GesStartResult Describes completed initialization independently of queue idleness. GesStringConstantSegment The immutable StringConstantSegment (section 0x0002): an ordered pool of at most 65,535 strict UTF-8 strings that bytecode and bindings reference by zero-based ushort index. Order and duplicates are program data. GesStringConstantSegment.SliceEntry Locates one string entry inside Data. GesUInt16IndexList A read-only view of one list of a GesUInt16IndexListSegment, such as an argument register list or a message shape; it shares the segment's storage without copying. GesUInt16IndexListSegment The immutable UInt16IndexListSegment (section 0x0003): at most 65,535 ordered lists of ushort elements that bindings and instructions reference by zero-based list index. The referencing field or opcode defines what the elements mean, for example string indices of argument names and tags, or register lists. GesUInt16IndexListSegment.SliceEntry Locates one list inside Data. GesVector A displacement with three Binary64 components and no unit, the native counterpart of a GES Vector. A 2D vector has Z 0. The unit belongs to the schema or host that uses the value and is applied when it converts to or from a GesValue. Interfaces IGesClock Supplies monotonic elapsed time to a serial host or a network end. Implementations must never move backwards. IGesExtensionFunction Synchronous host callback that implements one extension function. IGesExtensionRegistry Resolves the host's extension functions for the extension imports of a Program while Host.Load links it; it is not consulted per invocation. IGesExternalTypeCatalog Declarative compile-time description of the external types a host offers: names, fields and constructor signatures, without constructors, field accessors or host instances. IGesExternalTypeConstructor Host implementation of one declared external type constructor. IGesExternalTypeRegistry Resolves the host's external type constructors for the constructor imports of a Program while Host.Load links it; it is not consulted per call. IGesExternalValue A host object exposed to scripts as a value of a declared external type. The runtime keeps no field values: every script field read calls GetField(string) again, and every conversion to Map, JSON or schema encoding reads all declared fields in declaration order. IGesNativeMessageHandler Portable synchronous message handler invoked by a GameEventScriptHost. IGesProfiler Optional synchronous instrumentation factory. Callbacks must not throw or reenter a host. Timing, allocation and report policies belong to the embedding. Instances require serialized access. IGesProgramProfiler Instruction-boundary callbacks for one loaded instance. Callbacks must not throw, pump a host, or modify execution. No callback is made while the host waits between slices. IGesPublishSink Receives synchronous outbound publications after the host has attempted local enqueue. IGesRuntimeObserver Observes synchronous host behavior without participating in dispatch. Implementations must not throw and must not recursively pump the observed host. Every queued emit, processed publish, received message, delayed send and initialization message carries a host-local send ID: it starts at 1, increases by one per such send and is reported by every callback about that send, from emit, publish or scheduling to each dispatch or discard. 0 reports a send without an ID. Every callback has an empty default implementation, so an observer implements only the callbacks it needs. Enums GesBinaryBindKind Identifies the role of a GesBindingSegment entry: an executable declaration, an outbound message signature or a host import. GesBytecodeOpCode Identifies a V1 bytecode instruction. The numeric values are part of the .gesb format; operand layouts and semantics are defined in the bytecode specification. GesBytecodePatternKind Identifies the dice pattern of HasPattern and TakePattern. GesBytecodeSeriesKind Identifies a built-in lazy numeric series for CreateSeries. GesBytecodeTypeKind Identifies portable value kinds and VM-internal storage kinds used as bytecode type operands. GesDebugInfoOptions Selects which optional debug sections the Compiler emits. Compilation includes all of them by default; size-sensitive builds opt out with None. GesDebugSymbolKind The kind of a named register in GesDebugSymbolsSegment; the numeric values are the encoded SymbolKind byte. GesDiagnosticPhase Identifies the pipeline stage in which a diagnostic originated; the numeric values are stable. GesDiagnosticSymbolKind Identifies the role of the optional symbol named by a diagnostic. GesDocumentSchemaKind The kind of schema a GES document references. GesExecutionState Identifies why a synchronous host pump returned. GesNetworkClass The delivery class of a network route. GesNetworkSide The side a network route starts from. GesNetworkVerb How a network route carries its root. GesProfilePhase Non-overlapping regions of an instrumented VM loop; timing policies belong to the embedding. GesProgramFormatErrorCode The stable portable error codes of GesProgramFormatException. The numeric values are fixed by the binary format specification; the diagnostic code is decode. followed by the camel-case name. GesProgramRetention Selects which optional sections Read(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, GesProgramReadOptions?) keeps. The five required runtime sections are always read, and an unknown section flagged as required always fails. GesQuantityUnit Defines the supported game event script bytecode instruction unit values. GesSchemaDefaultKind The kinds of a field's default. GesSchemaKind The kinds of declarations that have a hash and can be bound. GesSchemaTypeKind The kinds of types a schema field can have. GesSectionFlags The SectionFlags word of a section header. Bits outside Required and CompressionMask are invalid in V1. GesSectionType The assigned .gesb section type IDs, listed in canonical writer order. Types 0x0000 and 0xFFFF are invalid; 0x8000–0xFFFD are free for private or experimental optional sections. GesStartState Identifies the outcome of host or instance initialization.

api/GameEventScript.Network.html.title: Namespace GameEventScript.Network | Game Event Script C# API — Unreleased (47afc43b2fc1)
api/GameEventScript.Network.html.summary: Namespace GameEventScript.Network Classes GesNetworkClientEnd The client end of a session: it owns one client connection and its transport and drives both from Poll<THandler>(ref THandler). Sends, publishes and ticks made before the session is established wait in the end and reach the connection when it connects. One caller at a time; not thread-affine. GesNetworkClientSecurity How a client protects its session: with the server's pinned public key, encrypted with a key the server sends during the handshake, or not at all. Immutable; safe to share between connections. GesNetworkCodes The codes a connection closes or cancels a transfer with. Each is stable and language-neutral. GesNetworkConnection One side of a network session: a synchronous state machine without threads, sockets or clocks. The host passes received bytes and the current time, takes events and takes packets to transmit. Times are microseconds of a monotonic clock chosen by the host. Not thread-safe; one caller at a time. GesNetworkCookies The address validation gate of a datagram server: it answers a client it does not know without keeping state, so a forged source address gains no connection. A cookie is the time window number and an HMAC-SHA256 of it and the address with a secret key; the current and the previous window are valid. Not thread-safe; one caller at a time. GesNetworkKey A server's static X25519 key pair, which encrypts its sessions. The client receives the public key from outside the protocol and pins it. Immutable; safe to share between connections. GesNetworkOptions The limits and transport of one connection. Values are checked when a connection is created. GesNetworkPair A client end and a server end connected within one process, without sockets. A realtime pair runs on the system clock and moves packets when the ends poll. A synchronous pair runs on a virtual clock, is connected when created and moves every packet before a send, publish, tick, close or poll returns: what one end sends is reported by the other end's next poll. In both modes a packet waits while the receiving connection takes no further bytes, in a synchronous pair until the host advances the clock far enough to refill its frame bucket; while 64 packets wait, the sending connection keeps its further packets. Both ends of a pair belong to one caller at a time. GesNetworkServerEnd The server end of a session: it accepts clients from an acceptor, owns one server connection per client and drives all of them from Poll<THandler>(ref THandler). Clients have stable end-local ids. Publishes and ticks reach every client. One caller at a time; not thread-affine. GesNetworkServerSecurity How a server protects its sessions: with its static key, or not at all. Immutable; safe to share between connections. GesNetworkSimulator Connects a client and a server connection in one process with seeded latency. Each packet is delayed by the latency plus a draw from 0 to the jitter inclusive, but never arrives before a packet sent earlier in the same direction. Between datagram connections it may also lose, duplicate and reorder packets. Equal seeds, options and inputs give equal packets, events and times. The host takes the events of both connections between calls of Advance(long). Not thread-safe. Structs GesNetworkEndEvent One end event. The payload is borrowed and valid until the handler returns. GesNetworkEvent One connection event. The payload is borrowed from the connection and valid until the next event is taken. Interfaces IGesNetworkAcceptor Accepts the transports of a server end's clients. IGesNetworkConnector Opens the transport of a client end. IGesNetworkEndHandler Receives the events of an end during its poll. IGesNetworkLink One connection's transport as an end drives it: it passes received packets to the connection and hands the connection's packets to the transport. Implementations come from a connector or an acceptor. Enums GesNetworkCookieResult What a server does with a datagram from an address it does not know. GesNetworkEndEventKind The kind of an end event. GesNetworkEventKind The kind of a connection event. GesNetworkSecurity The security level of a session. GesNetworkSendStatus The result of sending a payload on a route. GesNetworkState The state of a connection. GesNetworkTransport How a transport carries packets.

Returns string The value text. Returns bool true for every number, Boolean, Tag, Vector, Point, Handler, Message and external value, including zero and false; false for Nothing and for an empty Text, Dice, Bytes, List, Map, Record or Range. api/GameEventScript.Runtime.Values.html.summary: Namespace GameEventScript.Runtime.Values Classes GesValueMap The immutable Text-keyed entries of a Map or the fields of a Record, with unique keys sorted by Unicode scalar values; indexing and enumeration follow that canonical order. Structs GesValue An immutable GES value: Nothing, a number with optional quantity unit, Boolean, Text, Tag, Vector, Point, Dice, Bytes, List, Map, Record, external value, Range, Series, Message or Handler. Equality is strict and structural. GesValueArguments Ordered arguments of an extension call or external type constructor. A view lent by the virtual machine reads the caller's registers without copying and is valid only during that extension call: once the call has returned, every value access throws InvalidOperationException while Length stays unchanged. Copy any value needed later. A view created from an array borrows that array. GesValueMap.Enumerator Enumerates the entries of a GesValueMap in canonical key order. GesValueSlice Read-only view of a contiguous run of values, for example the elements of a List returned by AsList(). The view borrows its storage without copying; indexers return read-only references into that storage.
